The initial post was published on April 4, with a follow-up post on April 13.The posts included photos of the improvised devices, which appear to be made from black pieces of rubber or plastic with nails or screws poked through them. The fire department provided the following tips for residents:Use extra caution when traveling through the area.Avoid any suspicious objects in the roadway.Do not attempt to handle or remove these devices yourself.Anyone with information about the devices is asked to call the Phelps County Sheriff's Department. I was also curious, so I asked Emma Seymour, the associate director of the Textiles, Paper & Apparel Lab, what the real reason for those bath towel lines is. She told me that it's called a "dobby border" and explained why most (though not all) bath towels have them. If you've got towels on the brain, you can also check out our collection of clever uses for old towels and find out why textiles pros say you should never use a bath towel at the beach. Of course, we also have plenty of recommendations for the best bath towels, the best quick-dry towels, and the best Turkish towels. Below, Seymour explains exactly why your bath towels have those lines. What's the purpose of a towel line? "It's the dobby border, common on many bath towels," says Seymour. "It helps the towel keep its shape because it offers more structure than if it was entirely terrycloth. It also helps prevent fraying."What is a dobby border?A dobby border is a woven strip near a towel's ends. It can appear as a single strip or multiple, but it is always located near a towel's edges.According to Seymour, "Testers tend to like the look of the border, but most don't comment on it if a towel lacks a dobby border," meaning it's not a make-or-break feature for most customers.Do towels need a dobby border?Not necessarily. A towel without a dobby border will still absorb, as is its primary function. However, it may not have the same durability and longevity as one with a dobby border. It's about weighing out what's most important to you when shopping. If the price is right, and you like the look of a towel without a dobby border, buy it. There are other factors that contribute to a towel's durability and performance, such as fiber content, fabric weight, construction and more, not just the dobby border. So the towel you select may still go the distance. Our textiles pro filled us in on the real reason bath towels have those lines.
